newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar weaker at midsession but off lows.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar weaker at midsession but off lows.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures were trading lower at midsession on Monday as producer pricing outweighed follow-through speculative buying, market sources said.

Prices climbed to lifetime highs across the board on Friday as the speculators ran through a series of buy stops. Despite follow-through buying on the today's open, the benchmark October contract failed to reach the contract high of 11.93 cents made on Friday.
Trading sources said the market was staging a brief technical correction but the overall trend remains to the upside.
Resistance basis October was pegged at 11.93 cents followed by 12.00 cents.

"The market is in an uptrend that seems to be helped along by Russian buying and rumors of Indonesian buying," a broker said. Earlier today, however, traders in Indonesia said the country could import between 1.0 million and 1.1 million tonnes of mixed sugar in 1997, nearly unchanged from last year.
At 1125 EDT, CSCE benchmark October sugar stood 0.05 cent weaker at 11.81 cents a pound, having ranged from 11.89 to 11.72 cents. The rest of the board was trading 0.03 to 0.07 cent lower.
Trade selling was noted in the October/March spread, which stood at 0.18 cent at 1125 EDT, unchanged from Friday.
An estimated 10,059 lots changed hands as of 1100 EDT.
